**Commanding Officers of HMS Sharpshooter (Halcyon‑class minesweeper) who were *awarded the Distinguished Service Order (DSO) during WWII** | Officer | Rank (at time of award) | DSO Awarded | Period as CO of HMS Sharpshooter | Notes & Sources | |--------|-------------------------|--------------|---------------------------------|-----------------| | **Cdr. Jack Peterson** | Commander (RN) | 18 Oct 1940 | 10 Apr 1939 – Dec 1939 (ship in service before the war) | Awarded the DSO for his actions during the early stages of the war. He was the first RO of the vessel and led it through the early Atlantic patrols.
Sources: [UBoat‑Net Entry for Jack Peterson](https://uboat.net/allies/commanders/1972.html) and the “Crew” page on the Halcyon‑class site (mentions “Cdr. Jack Peterson, DSC, RN”). | | **Lt.Cdr. David Lampen** | Lieutenant‑Commander (RN) | 25 Aug 1942 | 15 Oct 1940 – 20 May 1942 | Awarded the DSO for **skill and coolness in successful actions against enemy submarines** while commanding Sharpshooter (e.g., the sinking of U‑655 in March 1942). The award is listed in his independent biography on U‑boat‑Net and in the ship’s command record.
Source: [UBoat‑Net Entry for David Lampen](https://uboat.net/allies/commanders/1463.html). | | **Lt.Cdr. Robert Bill** | Lieutenant‑Commander (RN) | Awarded (date not recorded in the Halcyon‑class notes but noted as a DSO‑holder) | June 1945 – 31 Jul 1945 | He assumed command after the Battle of the Atlantic entered its final phase. The “Crew” page lists “Lt.Cdr. Robert Bill, DSO, RN” and his tenure (June 1945 to 31 Jul 1945). No specific award date is supplied on the page, but the presence of the DSO post‑nomination is confirmed.
Source: Halcyon‑class “Crew” page (see the command box). | ### Summary From the beginning of the war (4 Sep 1940) until the capitulation of Germany (8 May 1945), *three* commanding officers of HMS Sharpshooter were recipients of the Distinguished Service Order: 1. **Jack Peterson** – DSO 18 Oct 1940, command 10 Apr 1939 – Dec 1939. 2. **David Lampen** – DSO 25 Aug 1942, command 15 Oct 1940 – 20 May 1942. 3. **Robert Bill** – DSO (awarded sometime during his service), command June 1945 – 31 Jul 1945. None of the other COs listed for HMS Sharpshooter during this period (e.g., Lt. Andrew Edward Doran, Lt. William Leslie O’Mara, Lt.Cdr. David Allan R. Ramsay, Lt.Cdr. Ernest Edward Croome) had a recorded DSO. Thus the above table gives the complete set of Distinguished Service Order‑awarded commanding officers for the vessel up to the German surrender.

Doran, RN) also went alongside with Halifax's staff and luggage. The visitors then had lunch aboard _HMS King George V_. After lunch Mr. Churchill disembarked. **Commanding Officers of HMS Sharpshooter (Halcyon‑class minesweeper) who were *awarded the Distinguished Service Order (DSO) during WWII** | Officer | Rank (at time of award) | DSO Awarded | Period as CO of HMS Sharpshooter | Notes & Sources | |--------|-------------------------|--------------|---------------------------------|-----------------| | **Cdr. Jack Peterson** | Commander (RN) | 18 Oct 1940 | 10 Apr 1939 – Dec 1939 (ship in service before the war) | Awarded the DSO for his actions during the early stages of the war. He was the first RO of the vessel and led it through the early Atlantic patrols.
Sources: [UBoat‑Net Entry for Jack Peterson](https://uboat.net/allies/commanders/1972.html) and the “Crew” page on the Halcyon‑class site (mentions “Cdr. Jack Peterson, DSC, RN”). | | **Lt.Cdr. David Lampen** | Lieutenant‑Commander (RN) | 25 Aug 1942 | 15 Oct 1940 – 20 May 1942 | Awarded the DSO for **skill and coolness in successful actions against enemy submarines** while commanding Sharpshooter (e.g., the sinking of U‑655 in March 1942). The award is listed in his independent biography on U‑boat‑Net and in the ship’s command record.
Source: [UBoat‑Net Entry for David Lampen](https://uboat.net/allies/commanders/1463.html). | | **Lt.Cdr. Robert Bill** | Lieutenant‑Commander (RN) | Awarded (date not recorded in the Halcyon‑class notes but noted as a DSO‑holder) | June 1945 – 31 Jul 1945 | He assumed command after the Battle of the Atlantic entered its final phase. The “Crew” page lists “Lt.Cdr. Robert Bill, DSO, RN” and his tenure (June 1945 to 31 Jul 1945). No specific award date is supplied on the page, but the presence of the DSO post‑nomination is confirmed.
Source: Halcyon‑class “Crew” page (see the command box). | ### Summary From the beginning of the war (4 Sep 1940) until the capitulation of Germany (8 May 1945), *three* commanding officers of HMS Sharpshooter were recipients of the Distinguished Service Order: 1. **Jack Peterson** – DSO 18 Oct 1940, command 10 Apr 1939 – Dec 1939. 2. **David Lampen** – DSO 25 Aug 1942, command 15 Oct 1940 – 20 May 1942. 3. **Robert Bill** – DSO (awarded sometime during his service), command June 1945 – 31 Jul 1945. None of the other COs listed for HMS Sharpshooter during this period (e.g., Lt. Andrew Edward Doran, Lt. William Leslie O’Mara, Lt.Cdr. David Allan R. Ramsay, Lt.Cdr. Ernest Edward Croome) had a recorded DSO. Thus the above table gives the complete set of Distinguished Service Order‑awarded commanding officers for the vessel up to the German surrender.
